'''Konda Gobyoyama Kofun''' (誉田御廟山古墳) or '''Kondayama Kofun''' (誉田山古墳) is a [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino, Osaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]], Japan. It is a keyhole-shaped Kofun and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Group]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:World Heritage Site|World Heritage Site]].
While the actual individual buried at the site is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] designates it as the tomb of the 15th emperor, [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]], and refers to it as "Ega no Mofushi no Oka no Misazagi" (惠我藻伏崗陵). It is also commonly called the "Emperor Ōjin Mausoleum." This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], Osaka.
On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in [[:en:Baku|Baku]], Azerbaijan.
{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of [[:en:Emperor Kinmei|Emperor Kinmei]] (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of [[:en:Mimana|Mimana]]. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}
The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].
== Overview ==
=== built and location === The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early [[:en:5th century|5th century]]. Its location spans across stable [[:en:Terrace_(geology)|terrace]] land and the unstable [[:en:Floodplain|Floodplain]], resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>
=== area === The official area, as published by Habikino City, are as follows:<ref>[http://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/10kakuka/34shakaikyoiku/03bunkazai/04isekishokai/04chuki/t_c_oujin.html 応神天皇陵古墳] (Habikino City website, updated June 14, 2012).</ref> * Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters * Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters * Rear Circle Height: 35 meters * Front Section Width: 300 meters * Front Section Height: 36 meters
Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>
=== Moats === The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.
=== burial goods === burial goods excavated include numerous [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>
== Associated Mounds == Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include: * '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods. * '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor. * '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|national treasures]].
== Shrine and Adjacent Features == * Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest [[:en:Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]]. * The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] maintains an office on-site for administration and preservation.

'''Konda Gobyoyama Kofun''' (誉田御廟山古墳) or '''Kondayama Kofun''' (誉田山古墳) is a [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a keyhole-shaped Kofun and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|en|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|WD=Q4250076|lt=Furuichi Kofun Group}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Heritage Site|en|World Heritage Site|WD=Q9259|lt=World Heritage Site}}.

While the actual individual buried at the site is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the tomb of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}}, and refers to it as "Ega no Mofushi no Oka no Misazagi" (惠我藻伏崗陵). It is also commonly called the "Emperor Ōjin Mausoleum." This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|WD=Q193428|lt=Sakai}}, Osaka.

On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in {{ill|Baku|en|Baku|WD=Q9248|lt=Baku}}, Azerbaijan.

{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei}} (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|WD=Q1790223|lt=Mimana}}. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}

The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].

== Overview ==

=== built and location ===
The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|WD=Q8095|lt=5th century}}. Its location spans across stable {{ill|Terrace_(geology)|en|Terrace_(geology)|WD=Q828581|lt=terrace}} land and the unstable {{ill|Floodplain|en|Floodplain|WD=Q193110|lt=Floodplain}}, resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

=== area ===
The official area, as published by Habikino City, are as follows:<ref>[http://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/10kakuka/34shakaikyoiku/03bunkazai/04isekishokai/04chuki/t_c_oujin.html 応神天皇陵古墳] (Habikino City website, updated June 14, 2012).</ref>
* Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters
* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters
* Rear Circle Height: 35 meters
* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>

=== Moats ===
The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:
* '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods.
* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|WD=Q1139795|lt=national treasures}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==
* Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine}}.
* The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} maintains an office on-site for administration and preservation.

'''Konda Gobyoyama Kofun''' (誉田御廟山古墳) or '''Kondayama Kofun''' (誉田山古墳) is a [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a keyhole-shaped Kofun and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|en|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|WD=Q4250076|lt=Furuichi Kofun Group}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Heritage Site|en|World Heritage Site|WD=Q9259|lt=World Heritage Site}}.

While the actual individual buried at the site is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the tomb of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}}, and refers to it as "Ega no Mofushi no Oka no Misazagi" (惠我藻伏崗陵). It is also commonly called the "Emperor Ōjin Mausoleum." This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|WD=Q193428|lt=Sakai}}, Osaka.

On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in {{ill|Baku|en|Baku|WD=Q9248|lt=Baku}}, Azerbaijan.

{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei}} (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|WD=Q1790223|lt=Mimana}}. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}

The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].

== Overview ==

=== built and location ===
The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|WD=Q8095|lt=5th century}}. Its location spans across stable {{ill|Terrace_(geology)|en|Terrace_(geology)|WD=Q828581|lt=terrace}} land and the unstable {{ill|Floodplain|en|Floodplain|WD=Q193110|lt=Floodplain}}, resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters

* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:

* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|WD=Q1139795|lt=national treasures}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==

The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:
* '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods.
* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|WD=Q1139795|lt=national treasures}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==
* Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine}}.

'''Konda Gobyoyama Kofun''' (誉田御廟山古墳) or '''Kondayama Kofun''' (誉田山古墳) is a [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino, Osaka|1=Habikino}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a keyhole-shaped Kofun and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|en|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|WD=Q4250076|lt=Furuichi Kofun Group|1=Furuichi Kofun Cluster}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Heritage Site|en|World Heritage Site|WD=Q9259|lt=World Heritage Site|1=World Heritage Site}}.

While the actual individual buried at the site is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the tomb of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin|1=Emperor Ōjin}}, and refers to it as "Ega no Mofushi no Oka no Misazagi" (惠我藻伏崗陵). It is also commonly called the "Emperor Ōjin Mausoleum." This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|WD=Q193428|lt=Sakai|1=Sakai}}, Osaka.

On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in {{ill|Baku|en|Baku|WD=Q9248|lt=Baku|1=Baku}}, Azerbaijan.

{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}} (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|WD=Q1790223|lt=Mimana|1=Mimana}}. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}

The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].

== Overview ==

=== built and location ===
The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|WD=Q8095|lt=5th century|1=5th century}}. Its location spans across stable {{ill|Terrace_(geology)|en|Terrace_(geology)|WD=Q828581|lt=terrace|1=Terrace (geology)}} land and the unstable {{ill|Floodplain|en|Floodplain|WD=Q193110|lt=Floodplain|1=Floodplain}}, resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

=== area ===

* Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters
* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters
* Rear Circle Height: 35 meters
* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>

=== Moats ===
The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:
* '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods.
* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|WD=Q1139795|lt=national treasures|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==
* Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}}.
* The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} maintains an office on-site for administration and preservation.

Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

=== area ===
The official area, as published by Habikino City, are as follows:<ref>[http://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/10kakuka/34shakaikyoiku/03bunkazai/04isekishokai/04chuki/t_c_oujin.html 応神天皇陵古墳] (Habikino City website, updated June 14, 2012).</ref>
* Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters
* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters
* Rear Circle Height: 35 meters
* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>

=== Moats ===
The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

'''Konda Gobyoyama Kofun''' (誉田御廟山古墳) or '''Kondayama Kofun''' (誉田山古墳) is a [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino, Osaka|1=Habikino}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a keyhole-shaped Kofun and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|en|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|WD=Q4250076|lt=Furuichi Kofun Group|1=Furuichi Kofun Cluster}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Heritage Site|en|World Heritage Site|WD=Q9259|lt=World Heritage Site|1=World Heritage Site}}.

While the actual individual buried at the site is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the tomb of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin|1=Emperor Ōjin}}, and refers to it as "Ega no Mofushi no Oka no Misazagi" (惠我藻伏崗陵). It is also commonly called the "Emperor Ōjin Mausoleum." This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|WD=Q193428|lt=Sakai|1=Sakai}}, Osaka.

On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in {{ill|Baku|en|Baku|WD=Q9248|lt=Baku|1=Baku}}, Azerbaijan.

{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}} (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|WD=Q1790223|lt=Mimana|1=Mimana}}. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}

The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].

The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].

== Overview ==

=== built and location ===
The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|WD=Q8095|lt=5th century|1=5th century}}. Its location spans across stable {{ill|Terrace_(geology)|en|Terrace_(geology)|WD=Q828581|lt=terrace|1=Terrace (geology)}} land and the unstable {{ill|Floodplain|en|Floodplain|WD=Q193110|lt=Floodplain|1=Floodplain}}, resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

=== area ===
The official area, as published by Habikino City, are as follows:<ref>[http://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/10kakuka/34shakaikyoiku/03bunkazai/04isekishokai/04chuki/t_c_oujin.html 応神天皇陵古墳] (Habikino City website, updated June 14, 2012).</ref>
* Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters
* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters
* Rear Circle Height: 35 meters
* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>

=== Moats ===
The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:
* '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods.
* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|WD=Q1139795|lt=national treasures|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==
* Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}}.
* The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} maintains an office on-site for administration and preservation.

This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|qid=Q193428|lt=Sakai|1=Sakai}}, Osaka.

On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in {{ill|Baku|en|Baku|qid=Q9248|lt=Baku|1=Baku}}, Azerbaijan.

{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|qid=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}} (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|qid=Q1790223|lt=Mimana|1=Mimana}}. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}

== Overview ==

=== built and location ===
The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|qid=Q8095|lt=5th century|1=5th century}}. Its location spans across stable {{ill|Terrace_(geology)|en|Terrace_(geology)|qid=Q828581|lt=terrace|1=Terrace (geology)}} land and the unstable {{ill|Floodplain|en|Floodplain|qid=Q193110|lt=Floodplain|1=Floodplain}}, resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

=== area ===
The official area, as published by Habikino City, are as follows:<ref>[http://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/10kakuka/34shakaikyoiku/03bunkazai/04isekishokai/04chuki/t_c_oujin.html 応神天皇陵古墳] (Habikino City website, updated June 14, 2012).</ref>
* Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters
* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters
* Rear Circle Height: 35 meters
* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>

=== Moats ===
The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|qid=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:
* '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods.
* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|qid=Q1139795|lt=national treasures|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==
* Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|qid=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}}.
* The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} maintains an office on-site for administration and preservation.

'''Konda Gobyoyama Kofun''' (誉田御廟山古墳) or '''Kondayama Kofun''' (誉田山古墳) is a [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino, Osaka|1=Habikino}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a keyhole-shaped Kofun and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|en|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qid=Q4250076|lt=Furuichi Kofun Group|1=Furuichi Kofun Cluster}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Heritage Site|en|World Heritage Site|qid=Q9259|lt=World Heritage Site|1=World Heritage Site}}.

While the actual individual buried at the site is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the tomb of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin|1=Emperor Ōjin}}, and refers to it as "Ega no Mofushi no Oka no Misazagi" (惠我藻伏崗陵). It is also commonly called the "Emperor Ōjin Mausoleum." This kofun is the second largest in Japan, following the {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|qid=Q193428|lt=Sakai|1=Sakai}}, Osaka.

On September 26, 2008, the {{ill|Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|ja|百舌鳥・古市古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group|qq=}}, including Konda Gobyoyama Kofun and Daisen Kofun, was a11ed to Japan's World Heritage Tentative List. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee officially registered the kofun group as a cultural heritage site on July 6, 2019, during a meeting in {{ill|Baku|en|Baku|qid=Q9248|lt=Baku|1=Baku}}, Azerbaijan.

{{ill|Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11631426}} is located near it. According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established in the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|qid=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}} (559 CE) by imperial decree aimed at restoring the kingdom of {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|qid=Q1790223|lt=Mimana|1=Mimana}}. The shrine was initially a mausoleum established in front of Emperor Ōjin’s tomb and is considered the oldest Hachiman shrine.{{Sfn|Habikino City|2019}} However an alternative theory says [[Kaijin Shrine]] is the oldest [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]].<ref name="rambelli-2018a">{{Cite book|last=Rambelli|first=F|title=The Sea and The Sacred in Japan|publisher=Bloomsbury Academic Publishing|year=2018|isbn=978-1350062870|location=Camden|pages=preface}}</ref>{{Rp|page=97–99}}

The name Gobyo comes from the honorific particle {{ill|御|lt=御 (Mi, O, Go)|ja|御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/御|1=御|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11488760}} and [[:en:Miao Shrine|byo shrine]].

== Overview ==

=== built and location ===
The Konda Gobyoyama Kofun was constructed in the early {{ill|5th century|en|5th century|qid=Q8095|lt=5th century|1=5th century}}. Its location spans across stable {{ill|Terrace_(geology)|en|Terrace_(geology)|qid=Q828581|lt=terrace|1=Terrace (geology)}} land and the unstable {{ill|Floodplain|en|Floodplain|qid=Q193110|lt=Floodplain|1=Floodplain}}, resulting in uneven ground conditions. The uneven moat and interior embankment are thought to have been influenced by the pre-existing {{ill|Futatsuzuka Kofun|ja|二ツ塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futatsuzuka Kofun|qq=}}. Landslides in the front section of the kofun are believed to have occurred during earthquakes in 734 and 1510 due to its proximity to the {{ill|Ikoma Fault Zone|ja|生駒断層帯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikoma Fault Zone|qq=}}.<ref group="Note">Geological surveys have identified active faults near the site, supporting this hypothesis.</ref>

=== area ===
The official area, as published by Habikino City, are as follows:<ref>[http://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/10kakuka/34shakaikyoiku/03bunkazai/04isekishokai/04chuki/t_c_oujin.html 応神天皇陵古墳] (Habikino City website, updated June 14, 2012).</ref>
* Mound Length: Approximately 425 meters
* Rear Circle Diameter: 250 meters
* Rear Circle Height: 35 meters
* Front Section Width: 300 meters
* Front Section Height: 36 meters

Debate persists over which part constitutes the base of the mound, resulting in varied measurements across studies.<ref group="Note">Examples of differing measurements are provided in historical records and archaeological research.</ref>

=== Moats ===
The kofun features a double moat system. The inner moat is surrounded by a central embankment approximately 48 meters wide, while the outer moat, initially around 35 meters wide, is encircled by an embankment approximately 15 meters wide.<ref name="oujinsoto">[[#堀江|Horie, "Ōjin Tennōryō Kofun Gaikō Gaitei" (1991), p. 248]]</ref> Water depths range from 1.7 to 2.5 meters, significantly deeper than the moats of the Daisen Kofun.

=== burial goods ===
burial goods excavated include numerous {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|qid=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}}, such as cylindrical haniwa, house-shaped haniwa, and figurines of shields, armor, and animals. Marine-themed clay figurines depicting whales, squid, and dolphins were also found in the inner moat. These findings suggest ritual significance tied to the sea.<ref name="oujinsoto"/>

== Associated Mounds ==
Several associated mounds (陪墳) are identified around the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun. Notable examples include:
* '''Tatezuka Kofun''' – A scallop-shaped mound containing numerous shields and high-quality burial goods.
* '''Shukin-zuka Kofun''' – A square mound featuring gold burial goods and armor.
* '''Konda Maruyama Kofun''' – A round mound with horse gear Historic Site1 as {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|qid=Q1139795|lt=national treasures|1=National Treasure (Japan)}}.

== Shrine and Adjacent Features ==
* Adjacent to the kofun lies {{ill|Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|lt=Konda Hachimangū|ja|誉田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Hachimangū|1=Konda Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11631426}}, Japan's oldest {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|qid=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman Shrine|1=Hachiman shrine}}.
* The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} maintains an office on-site for administration and preservation.
